steps.title: Open the Data Manager
steps.narration: Let's start on the Data Manager page, where the app shows exactly how much market data it has and lets you grow it on demand.
steps.point_out: The Dataset coverage panel is already filled in with real figures — Universe, Symbols, Trading days, Snapshot dates, and Backfill gaps — nothing blank and nothing stuck loading.

steps.title: Pick a job type
steps.narration: The "Job kind" dropdown offers three plain-language choices for growing the dataset. Let's pick "Fetch EOD prices" first.
steps.point_out: As soon as a fetch-style job is chosen, an "Import source" dropdown appears, since a fetch needs to know where to pull prices from.

steps.title: Switch to a backfill job
steps.narration: Now let's switch to "Backfill snapshots" instead, since that's the job we'll actually run next.
steps.point_out: The Import source dropdown disappears again — the form only ever asks for what the chosen job actually needs.

steps.title: Run a backfill job
steps.narration: With a real multi-day range already filled in from the app's own list of gaps, clicking Start kicks off the job.
steps.point_out: A plain-language breakdown appears — how many calendar days, how many were already covered, how many weren't trading days — and a "Refreshed" note lists exactly which stored figures this run kept current, with the Snapshot dates and Backfill gaps tiles above updating to match, no reload needed.

steps.title: Check the run history
steps.narration: Scrolling down to the Run history table shows a permanent log of every job that's ever run.
steps.point_out: This run's row carries the exact same "Refreshed" note — proof it's a durable record, not just a one-time message that vanishes on reload.

steps.title: See input validation in action
steps.narration: Finally, let's see what happens if a date is mistyped. Typing an impossible date should be caught right away, before it can ever be submitted.
steps.point_out: A clear red message and warning icon appear immediately below the field explaining exactly what's wrong, and the Start button greys out until it's fixed.

expect.text: Enter a valid date as yyyy-MM-dd
